blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A service runs with -Xmx equal to its container's memory limit and keeps getting OOMKilled. Why?

options.text: Metaspace, thread stacks and direct buffers use memory outside the heap.
options.says: The container limit covers the whole process, so it has to sit well above -Xmx (the page says 20 to 30 percent) to leave room for non-heap memory.

options.text: The young generation is sized on top of -Xmx, so the heap passes the limit.
options.says: -Xmx bounds the whole heap, young generation included; the memory past the limit is outside the heap.

options.text: A full GC copies the old generation into memory reserved beyond -Xmx.
options.says: The page puts the extra memory in Metaspace, thread stacks and direct buffers, not in a copy made by the collector.

questions.stem: Why is running jmap -histo:live <pid> against a production JVM risky?

options.text: Its :live option writes a full heap dump to disk before printing the histogram.
options.says: A histogram only counts objects per class; writing a dump is what jmap -dump or jcmd GC.heap_dump does.

options.text: Its :live option forces a full GC, so that unreachable objects are left out.
options.says: The :live option collects first, pausing the application; jmap -histo without it, or jcmd GC.class_histogram -all, skips the GC.

options.text: Its :live option switches the JVM to the Serial collector until it restarts.
options.says: No diagnostic command changes the collector; the collector is fixed when the JVM starts.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: jmap -histo:live and a plain jcmd GC.class_histogram force a full GC, so production histograms use the variants that skip it.
A container is OOMKilled when the whole JVM, heap plus Metaspace, stacks, code cache and direct memory, exceeds its limit, so the limit must leave room above -Xmx.
